paragraph: Elmwood Park's single-family market is the volume, with 41 sales over six months at a median of $625,000 and a sale-to-list ratio of 1.02. Two thirds of those homes sold above asking with a median of 20 days on market, so it's competitive without being frenzied. The range runs from $320,000 to $1,400,000, which is wide enough that the median is the better guide than either end. Multi-family is the tighter market here. Thirteen sales at a median of $900,000, a sale-to-list ratio of 1.07, 17 days on market, and 12 of 13 selling above list. Sellers are dictating terms in that tier, and buyers should expect competition on anything well located. Condos and townhouses are thin at 8 sales, median $449,000, selling right at list price. That sample is too small to read closely. On the monthly numbers, volume built steadily from 4 closings in February to 8 and 9 in the summer months, which tracks the normal Bergen arc, while the month-to-month medians swing on mix rather than value. If the usual pattern holds, expect closing counts to ease through fall. If you're comparing tiers, the deciding factor isn't market heat. It's whether you want the space and grounds of a single-family, the rental income of a multi-family, or the lower maintenance of a condo.
